requirements.md:285 (BL-004) makes a claim about shared, git-tracked protected-file-list membership sourced from `guard_invariants.py:4`/`:18` and closes with an explicit instruction: 'Re-verify per the Assumptions section before relying on this.' requirements.md:286 (BL-005) makes the identical class of claim -- `.github/workflows/test.yml` is protected, 'same list, same read' from `guard_invariants.py:4` and `:18` -- but carries no equivalent re-verification trailer. The generic Assumptions-section bullet that is supposed to backstop this (requirements.md:274, 'Protected-file membership is shared, git-tracked state this branch does not own') explicitly names only 'BL-004's claim' as the thing that 'must be re-derived,' not BL-005's. Downstream failure mode: an implementer using requirements.md's own Assumptions section as the authoritative re-verification checklist (as the document frames it) could treat BL-005's protected-file/PHASE2_HUMAN_COPY_TARGETS claim as settled and skip re-deriving it at implementation start -- even though it is exactly the volatile, shared, git-tracked list AGENTS.md 'Author-time sweeps' item 3 requires re-verifying, and REQ-008(c)/BL-005's whole task-plan shape (a second staged, human-applied patch, not agent-writable) depends on that protection status holding. This belongs to spec review because it is a completeness defect in the requirements artifact's own re-verification instructions, not an implementation-architecture choice. (investigation.md:178's INV-014 table does carry a generic 'each target' re-derivation instruction that would incidentally cover `.github/workflows/test.yml`, but requirements.md -- the primary normative document -- does not carry that same coverage for BL-005 specifically, so the gap is real within the document under review.)

This feature is centrally about a human-approval/egress boundary, so SKIP does not apply. The boundary is comprehensively and testably specified at the document-conformance level this whole specification operates at (stated once, acceptance-tests.md:3): first-upload gating (AC-001/TEST-001, requirements.md:44), iteration (AC-001 branch2/TEST-002), scope re-gating (AC-001 branch3/TEST-003), the three-outcome resolution model including the denied outcome needed by #140 (AC-019/TEST-028-030, requirements.md:194-196), transient decline vs. persistent denial (AC-026/TEST-041-043), destination re-gating (AC-027/TEST-044-045) and mid-session withdrawal (AC-028/TEST-046-047). The specification also honestly discloses, rather than hides, that the Design-Source record is an unenforced audit trace (AC-012, requirements.md:156; TEST-018) -- this is an accurate description of the pre-existing prose-only enforcement architecture of the whole design-sync-loop skill (INV-019/INV-021, investigation.md:224-244), not a new gap this feature introduces, and the acceptance criteria make that honesty itself a testable requirement rather than an unstated assumption.

Of the four remaining open questions, OQ-6 is hedged by AC-005's stated-limitation requirement (requirements.md:96,110), OQ-9 is hedged by AC-018's non-interactive-by-design requirement (requirements.md:192) and is explicitly a future #139/#140 design question this feature only leaves room for (requirements.md:182), and OQ-10 is explicitly scoped to a sibling artifact ('touches no criterion here', requirements.md:322-323). OQ-7 (requirements.md:144,306) is the closest candidate: REQ-004 explicitly declines to decide the Design-Source 'upload subject' field's value-granularity, calling it 'a product decision.' However AC-010 (requirements.md:146-148) only requires the field be *named*, which is satisfiable independent of that decision, and per the calibration's Gate Responsibility ('do not require design decisions ... those belong to later gates'), granularity choice for a record's value format is a design-phase decision in this repository's own multi-document workflow (a design.md artifact exists downstream of this spec), not a product-behaviour gap the reviewer must invent from nothing -- REQ-004/OQ-7 already supplies the trade-off analysis (investigation.md:307) that later phase needs. No check ID in this specification is left unresolved by these four.

No `domain/` directory exists at the repository root (confirmed via directory listing of the repository root and of `specs/design-sync-consent/`), so the check's explicit skip condition ('When domain/ is absent ... record the check as skipped') applies.
